messages:
sachin: quick ping — I opened a tiny TF change to give payments-staging SA decrypt access to the invoices KMS key. noticed annotation propagation is slow in staging and wanna avoid breaking the rollout. plan shows a key grant + iam role update. can someone sanity-check the snippets?

maria: paste the tf pls, also which SA are you annotating?

sachin: the SA is `payments-ingest-staging` — snippet from the PR:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "payments_decrypt" {
  name       = "payments-staging-decrypt"
  key_id     = aws_kms_key.invoices.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.payments_ingest_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}

resource "kubernetes_service_account" "payments_ingest_sa" {
  metadata {
    name = "payments-ingest-staging"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.payments_ingest_irsa.arn
    }
  }
}
```

sachin: plan shows: 
- will create kms_grant.payments_decrypt
- will update k8s_service_account.payments_ingest_sa (annotation)

kevin: two quick things: 1) prefer granting the IAM principal (role) with a condition for `aws:SourceArn`/`aws:SourceAccount` so the grant is scoped if possible. 2) watch the apply ordering — if SA annotation updates before role trust is ready you can get pods failing to assume. recommend a short manual pause between steps or Terraform targets.

anna: optional: instead of modifying the key policy, a grant is good. but make sure the grant principal is the role *ARN* not the role ID. also add `operations = ["Decrypt", "DescribeKey"]` so future checks don't break.

maria: FYI staging OIDC can lag ~30s after SA annotate -> kubectrl shows annotation present but kube JWT signer not immediately accepted by AWS if role doc isn't synced. we had a race last month. either: apply key grant first, then role+sa, or add a small `sleep` in the pipeline between steps.

sachin: good notes — i'll update the grant to include DescribeKey and add a condition like you suggested. regarding ordering: i can split the PR into two commits so TF will apply grant first, then the SA annotation. is that ok?

kevin: yep split is ideal. also add a short note in the PR description: "apply grant first, wait 30s, then annotate SA". saves others from surprise.

deploy-bot: CI check — terraform plan (pr#5123) completed: 1 to add, 1 to change. no drift detected.

sachin: thanks — i'll push the split and tag y'all when ready. @maria @kevin @anna : if you can eyeball the updated grant after i push that'd be great. :thumbsup:

maria: ack, will look once you push.

kevin: ack, will review after lunch.

sachin: pushed split + updated grant, plan looks clean, scheduling apply to staging now. will monitor pods for ~5m and rollback if any assume failures.

deploy-bot: apply started (staging): tf apply in progress...

sachin: apply finished, pods restarted cleanly after ~40s, no assume failures seen. closing the thread.
